reason: The provided sources contain dozens of cross-verified facts across independent publications detailing Tiangong's origin, hardware, missions, and space telescope companion.
story: When US law barred China from participating in the International Space Station, China responded by building its own modular space station in orbit. After testing rendezvous and refueling techniques on precursor labs Tiangong-1 and Tiangong-2, China launched the Tianhe core module in April 2021. The first crew arrived aboard Shenzhou 12 in June 2021, and the addition of the Wentian and Mengtian experiment modules in 2022 completed the station. Orbiting roughly 400 kilometers above Earth, Tiangong permanently hosts three astronauts for six-month missions, expanding to six during crew handovers. Despite political barriers, Tiangong hosts research from 17 countries and previously included joint survival training with European Space Agency astronauts. To supercharge its research, China built Tiangong to companion with the Xuntian space telescope, which boasts a view 300 times wider than Hubble and is designed to dock with Tiangong for refueling and maintenance.
angle: After being banned from the ISS by US law, China built its own space station and a co-orbiting space telescope with a view 300 times wider than Hubble that docks with the station for repairs.

claims.claim: US law prohibit NASA from direct collaboration with China, barring Chinese astronauts from participating in the International Space Station.
China launched its first precursor space laboratory, Tiangong-1, in 2011 to test rendezvous and docking capabilities.
China launched Tiangong-2 in 2016 to test longer-term life support systems and orbital refueling.
Construction of the modular Tiangong space station began with the launch of the Tianhe core module in April 2021.
The first crewed mission to the Tiangong space station was Shenzhou 12, carrying three astronauts in June 2021.
China completed the basic configuration of Tiangong in 2022 by adding the Wentian and Mengtian experiment modules.
Tiangong permanently supports a core crew of three astronauts on six-month missions.
Tiangong can temporarily support up to six astronauts simultaneously during crew handover periods.
The China Manned Space Agency has tentatively approved more than 1,000 scientific experiments aboard Tiangong.
Tiangong hosts scientific experiments involving researchers from 17 countries.
European Space Agency astronauts have undertaken astronaut training, including survival training, alongside Chinese astronauts.
Cargo resupply missions to the Tiangong space station are conducted by autonomous Tianzhou spacecraft.
Tiangong operates in low Earth orbit at an altitude of approximately 340 to 450 kilometers.
The co-orbiting Xuntian space telescope is designed to periodically dock with Tiangong for servicing, refueling, and upgrades.
The Xuntian space telescope features a two-meter diameter primary mirror.
The survey camera on the Xuntian space telescope has a field of view more than 300 times larger than that of the Hubble Space Telescope.

disputed: Target launch date for the Xuntian space telescope shifted from 2023 in earlier sources to 2025 and 2027 in later sources; the script should refrain from stating a fixed past date or state 'scheduled for launch in the late 2020s'.

Compatibility of the Chinese Docking Mechanism with ISS ports is disputed between sources calling it an APAS clone versus claiming incompatibility; the script should omit technical docking mechanism compatibility debates.
